newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re sees Asian insurance market boom.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re sees Asian insurance market boom.

text.p: Asian insurance markets should expand at more than double the world average through 2000 as strong economic growth unlocks pent-up demand, Swiss Reinsurance Co said in a report.
Swiss Re said premium volume in the 11 biggest Asian markets excluding Japan was likely to grow by a real 10 percent per year from 1995 through 2000.
"Global premium volume is expected to increase by about four percent during the same period," the world's second biggest reinsurance group said in its latest Sigma research report.
The study covered the 12 most important Asian insurance markets -- China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.

Swiss Re cited forecasts that real annual Gross Domestic Product (GPD) in these countries, excepting Japan, will grow by 7.6 percent annually from 1995 through 2000 as against world expansion of 3.5 percent per year.
"In the insurance industry, growth rates will turn out even more in favour of Asia since several countries in the region have pent-up demand," it said.

"As a result, by the year 2000 Asia will boost its world share of GDP by 1.3 percent, of non-life premiums by 1.9 percent and of life insurance premiums -- due to the weak growth iun Japan -- by 0.7 percent," the report added.
Swiss Re said the Asian markets were better supplied than the world average for life insurance but below levels for non-life that would be expected based on income levels.
"The forecast predicts that the shortfall (in non-life insurance) will be made up only slowly," it said.
Life insurance was more popular mainly due to a high savings rate and the need to add on to relatively low state and company pensions.

Swiss Re said Asian markets were often difficult to access for foreign insurers but were expected to open in the long-term under minimum standards under the global GATT free trade pact of the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
